questions.text: National leaders should need to win regular competitive elections to remain in office.
Important national policy decisions should be delegated to independent experts who do not need approval from elected representatives for each decision.
Every adult citizen should have the right to vote, regardless of their education or intelligence.
During a serious emergency, the head of government should be able to put temporary laws into effect before parliament votes, with those laws expiring if parliament rejects them.
Parties opposing the government should be allowed to campaign and stand in national elections under the same conditions as the incumbent government.
Citizens should be able to put proposed national laws to a binding public vote by collecting enough signatures.
Courts independent of the government should be able to overturn government decisions that violate the constitution.
The governing party or coalition should be able to choose a new head of government between elections without holding a new public vote.
The governing leadership should have authority to exclude parties from national elections because of their political positions.
Voters should be able to repeal a law through a binding referendum.
An elected head of government should be able to make major policy decisions within existing law without obtaining parliament’s approval for each decision.
Elected representatives should be able to remove the head of government for serious abuse of power through a defined constitutional process.
Parliament should be able to postpone a scheduled national election during a serious emergency, for a limited period specified in law.
Voters should be able to remove an elected representative before their term ends through a defined recall vote.
National leaders should be able to govern without being accountable to voters or elected representatives.
The armed forces should be able to replace a civilian government on their own judgement that it is unfit to govern.
Adults should be allowed to make personal choices such as drug use that risk personal wellbeing when they do not directly harm others.
Authorities should be allowed to monitor private communications when a court authorises the surveillance to investigate serious crime.
Peaceful public demonstrations should be allowed even when they temporarily obstruct roads or access to businesses, provided emergency access remains available.
People should be allowed to criticise public institutions, even when their criticism causes widespread offence.
The government should be able to require adults to follow health measures intended primarily to protect those adults themselves.
Police should be allowed to keep records of people’s movements for several years, even when those people are not suspected of an offence.
Police should be allowed to stop drivers at random and test them for intoxication, even without a reason to suspect impairment.
Authorities should be able to restrict a person’s movements before they commit an offence when a court finds a serious risk that they will harm others.
Adults should be allowed to access books, films, and websites that the government considers morally objectionable.
People should be allowed to use online communication services without having to verify their identity with the government.
Police should be able to stop and search people without individual suspicion when there is a credible threat of serious violence in the area.
Authorities should be able to prohibit a public gathering when there is credible evidence that it is likely to lead to serious disorder.
Police should need a court warrant to search someone’s home without their consent, except when there is an immediate threat to someone’s safety.
People should be allowed to publish confidential government information that reveals official misconduct.
Adults should be allowed to own firearms for personal defence, subject to checks for a history of violence.
Authorities should be allowed to hold people suspected of terrorism without independent court review until they consider the threat resolved.
The government should prioritise the national culture over migrant cultures when they conflict.
Public services should accommodate different cultural practices, even when doing so requires additional public spending.
People who settle permanently in a country should be expected to adopt its cultural customs.
Becoming part of the national community should not require giving up a foreign cultural identity.
Public institutions should prioritise using the national language over providing services in several foreign languages.
National ceremonies should acknowledge Indigenous peoples within the nation, even when they make up a very small share of the population.
Government cultural funding should primarily support my country’s predominant traditions.
Distinct cultural identities should take priority over a shared national culture when their expectations conflict.
Public institutions should organise their schedules around one common cultural calendar rather than accommodate different communities’ celebrations.
The government should recognise several cultural traditions as part of my country’s national identity.
Integration programmes should encourage migrants to participate in the wider national community rather than live mainly within culturally separate communities.
Public signage should be written in foreign languages to accommodate migrants within their communities.
Families should give greater emphasis to a shared national identity than to a distinct community identity.
Full body coverings, such as the burqa, should remain legal even when other full body coverings are prohibited.
My country’s national identity should include several distinct cultural ways of life.
Government integration programmes should emphasise adopting shared national customs rather than maintaining distinct community customs.
Permanent immigration should be subject to a strict annual numerical limit, based on housing availability and workforce deficits.
People should generally be allowed to settle in another country to improve their living conditions.
Only applicants with skills considered important to my country should normally qualify for permanent residence.
Partners and dependent children of immigrants who are permanently settled in my country should generally be allowed to join them.
Refugees fleeing their home countries should be allowed to settle permanently, regardless of their skills or cultural compatibility.
People who migrate illegally should be allowed to remain in my country rather than face deportation.
Permanent immigration should be limited even when employers want to recruit more workers from abroad.
Immigration should be reduced to ease pressure on housing and public services, even when additional arrivals would bring economic benefits.
Family immigration should count towards the same annual numerical limit as other permanent immigration.
People with a confirmed job offer should generally be allowed to move to my country for work.
Applicants for permanent settlement should need sponsorship from an employer or family member.
Graduating from one of my country’s universities should not, by itself, provide a route to permanent residence.
People fleeing persecution should be allowed to enter and receive protection even when ordinary immigration limits have been reached.
The government should prioritise migrants from culturally similar countries.
My country should allow non-citizen migrants to receive welfare benefits or live in social housing.
My country should allow more migrants from diverse backgrounds because their cultures differ from our own.
My country should be willing to use military force to secure national interests, even when it has not been attacked.
Diplomatic measures should take priority over military action, even when they are slower to achieve my country’s aims.
My country should be willing to bear substantial financial costs to maintain military superiority over potential opponents.
Military action should be permitted to prevent an imminent attack when there is strong evidence that the attack is being prepared.
My country should use armed force only to respond to an armed attack against itself or an ally.
My country should require male citizens to complete a period of military service to train a large, capable force and deter potential aggressors.
My country should accept substantial diplomatic concessions to prevent a war, even when doing so weakens its international position.

My country should develop AI-powered weapons that can select and attack targets without a human approving each attack if this would make military operations more efficient and improve national security.
Defence policy should focus on repelling attacks rather than conducting military campaigns abroad.
My country should avoid war and military action at all costs, even if an ally is being attacked.
My country should maintain forces capable of prolonged combat beyond its borders.
My country should leave a territorial dispute unresolved rather than start a war to settle it.
My country should be willing to threaten military action to obtain concessions in serious international disputes.
When the two conflict, reducing the risk of war should take priority over demonstrating military resolve.
My country should use military espionage to gain an advantage over potential opponents, even when doing so risks worsening relations with them.
My country should accept reductions in its military capabilities as part of negotiated efforts to prevent war.
My country’s institutions should have final authority over laws that apply within its borders.
International institutions should have authority to make binding decisions for my country, even when my government opposes those decisions.
Courts in my country should have final authority when national law conflicts with an international court’s ruling.
My country should make long-term commitments to international alliances, even when those commitments limit its freedom to act independently.
My country should be able to withdraw from international commitments without needing approval from international institutions.
International courts should have binding authority over disputes involving my government, including cases brought against its own officials.
My country should prioritise its own interests when they conflict with goals set by international institutions.
Countries should give international institutions decision-making authority over environmental problems that cross national borders.
My country should remain outside international blocs that require members to adopt a common foreign policy.
International human-rights institutions should be able to require changes to my country’s laws.
My country should keep control of its currency rather than transfer monetary policy to a shared international authority.
My country should pool funding and decision-making with other countries to manage shared international problems.
My country should retain sole authority over entry at its borders rather than share that authority with international institutions.
My country should accept common trade rules negotiated with other countries rather than set all its trade rules independently.
My country should keep control of national policy rather than join an international political federation.
My country should join international efforts to enforce collectively agreed rules, even when staying neutral would better serve its immediate interests.
Most businesses in my country should be privately owned.
Essential utility networks in my country, such as water supply networks, should be publicly owned.
Private ownership should be preferred when public and private providers could offer comparable cost, quality, and access.
My country should establish publicly owned businesses in competitive industries rather than leave those industries entirely to private owners.
Healthcare facilities in my country should generally be privately owned, even when treatment is publicly funded.
Passenger rail infrastructure in my country should be publicly owned.
Publicly funded services should be contracted to privately owned providers when they can offer comparable quality and access at lower cost.
My country should have publicly owned banks alongside private banks.
My country should sell publicly owned commercial businesses to private owners.
Public bodies should own a substantial share of rental housing in my country.
Businesses important to national security should remain privately owned when government regulation can protect security interests.
Businesses extracting natural resources in my country should generally be publicly owned.
Public bodies should contract routine services, such as waste collection, to privately owned businesses rather than operate their own providers.
The government should retain ownership of strategic businesses even when selling them would raise substantial public revenue.
A publicly owned business that repeatedly needs financial support should be sold to private owners rather than kept in public ownership.
My country should own a national broadcaster rather than leave broadcasting entirely to private owners.
My country should use import tariffs to protect domestic businesses from foreign competition.
My country should remove most barriers to international trade, even when some domestic businesses lose sales.
My government should favour domestic suppliers when purchasing goods, even when foreign suppliers offer lower prices.
Businesses in my country should be free to buy goods and materials from whichever country offers the best terms.
My country should restrict imports of essential goods to preserve domestic production, even when imported goods cost less.
My country should reduce its own trade barriers even when other countries do not do the same.
My country should temporarily restrict imports to help new domestic industries become established, even when this raises prices for consumers.
Foreign investors should be allowed to establish businesses on the same terms as domestic investors, even when local firms face more competition.
My country should restrict agricultural imports to preserve domestic farming capacity.
Domestic businesses should adjust to foreign competition rather than receive government trade protection.
My country should impose tariffs in response to tariffs placed on its exports.
Foreign and domestic products should face the same product taxes in my country.
My country should restrict imports from foreign firms that receive large subsidies from their governments.
Trade agreements signed by my country should remove tariffs, even when this increases dependence on foreign suppliers.
My country should prevent foreign investors from gaining control of strategic businesses, even when they offer more investment than domestic buyers.
People in my country should be free to buy online services from foreign providers without special trade restrictions.
Businesses in my country should generally decide what to produce without government direction.
My government should set compulsory production targets for economically important industries.
Prices in my country should generally be determined by supply and demand rather than set by government.
My government should direct investment towards sectors chosen in a national economic plan.
Businesses in my country should expand or close according to consumer demand rather than government production plans.
My government should control the prices of essential goods, even when suppliers would prefer to charge more.
Businesses in my country should be able to enter an industry without having to prove to the government that more production is needed.
My government should direct banks to lend to industries it considers national priorities.
People and businesses should be able to move their money abroad without government approval.
My government should subsidise selected industries to steer economic development, even when private investors would favour other sectors.
Privately issued currencies should be allowed to compete with government-issued money.
My government should set a legal minimum wage rather than leave the lowest wages entirely to negotiation between employers and workers.
Wages in my country should generally be set through negotiations between employers and workers rather than government wage schedules.
My government should direct central-bank lending and interest-rate policy to support its national economic plan.
Rental prices in my country should be set by market demand rather than government rent controls.
My government should coordinate national production and distribution during ordinary economic conditions rather than leave them to individual businesses.
My country should use taxes and benefits to substantially reduce differences in disposable income.
Reducing income differences should not, by itself, justify taking more income through taxation.
My country should provide a stronger minimum income through benefits, even when this requires higher taxes.
Income benefits should provide a basic safety net rather than substantially narrow differences in living standards.
Higher earners in my country should pay a substantially larger share of their income in tax than lower earners.
People in my country should retain more of their earnings, even if this leaves larger income differences between households.
My country should tax large inheritances to fund income support for people with fewer resources.
Income support for working-age adults who can work should have a time limit, even if some recipients still have low incomes when it ends.
My country should tax accumulated wealth to fund transfers to households with low incomes.
Income benefits should be kept modest so that those funding them face a lower tax burden.
People eligible for income benefits should receive enough support to participate in ordinary social life, beyond meeting basic survival needs.
My country should prioritise cutting taxes over increasing cash benefits.
My country should provide publicly funded income supplements to low-paid workers.
Additional income earned by high earners should not face higher tax rates than additional income earned by other workers.
My country should redistribute some large landholdings to people with little or no land, compensating owners through public funds.
Cash benefits should be restricted to households unable to meet basic needs rather than extended to a wider range of low-income households.
My country’s laws should be justified without relying on the teachings of any particular religion.
Religious teachings should be an official source of national law in my country.
My government should make policy without needing approval from religious leaders.
My country’s constitution should recognise a particular religion as a foundation of the state.
Public schools in my country should teach about religions without trying to persuade pupils to adopt one.
Public schools in my country should include instruction intended to cultivate faith in the state’s recognised religion.
My country’s state courts should apply laws enacted by civil institutions rather than rulings issued by religious authorities.
Religious authorities should have an official role in reviewing proposed laws before my government enacts them.
Official ceremonies held by my government should not include organised religious worship.
My government should use public funds for activities intended to strengthen religious belief.
Government buildings should not display symbols endorsing a particular religion.
My country should keep national public holidays marking the predominant religion’s major festivals as an official recognition of that religion.
Religious leaders should not hold government seats solely because of their religious office.
Religious organisations should receive tax exemptions specifically for their religious activities, beyond exemptions available for charitable work.
My country should remove religious approval requirements from laws governing marriage.
My country should recognise decisions made by religious courts as legally binding in some areas of family law.
Social customs in my country should be open to substantial change as people’s values change.
Preserving long-standing social traditions should take priority over adapting them to new values.
Families outside the traditional two-parent married household should receive the same social recognition as that household.
Society should continue to encourage distinct traditional roles for men and women.
Marriage in my country should be available to couples regardless of their sex.
Society should continue to favour the two-parent married household as its preferred family model.
Choosing an abortion early in pregnancy should be socially accepted.
Parents should have the final say over whether their children receive school lessons that conflict with the family’s traditional sexual values.
Same-sex couples should be as socially accepted as adoptive parents as opposite-sex couples.
Traditional expectations about modest dress should continue to guide how people dress in public.
Language conventions should change to reflect how people identify themselves, even when this departs from traditional usage.
Passing established moral customs to the next generation should take priority over encouraging new ones.
Adults who take on roles traditionally associated with the other sex should receive the same social acceptance as those who follow traditional roles.
Changes to long-standing social institutions should be gradual, even when faster change is popular.
Schools should teach pupils about different sexual orientations and gender identities, even when these differ from traditional family expectations.
Long-standing customs should be preserved for their connection to earlier generations, even when their practical purpose is no longer clear.
My country should allow new technologies to be widely used when early evidence suggests substantial benefits, even if long-term risks remain uncertain.
New technologies should remain limited to small trials until there is substantial evidence about their long-term risks.
My country should approve major infrastructure projects when their public benefits are substantial, even if some natural habitats are permanently lost.
New medical technologies should not become widely available until their long-term safety has been studied.
My country should adopt AI systems that raise workplace productivity, even if many existing jobs are replaced and workers must retrain.
Preserving undisturbed habitats should take priority over development projects, even when the projects would bring substantial public benefits.
My country should support replacing some conventional meat production with cultivated meat, even before its long-term environmental effects are fully understood.
Brain implants intended to enhance the abilities of healthy people should remain limited to research until there is strong evidence of long-term safety.
My country should prioritise technological solutions to climate change over reducing energy and material consumption, even when those technologies are not yet proven at large scale.
Major construction projects should be delayed while their environmental effects remain poorly understood, even when the projects are expected to benefit the public.
Adults should be allowed to use brain implants to enhance their mental abilities once basic safety requirements are met, even if long-term effects remain uncertain.
AI systems used to make medical diagnoses should remain limited to supervised trials until there is strong evidence of their reliability across different patient groups.
My country should allow controlled trials of embryo gene editing to enhance human abilities, rather than limit gene editing to preventing disease.
Genetically modified crops should require evidence of long-term ecosystem safety before widespread cultivation, even if early trials show higher yields.
My country should prioritise expanding housing and transport infrastructure over preserving undeveloped land when the two conflict.
My country should delay technologies that could cause irreversible harm until there is strong evidence that the harm is unlikely, even when early evidence suggests substantial benefits.
States and regions should have a protected right to govern their own affairs, even when the national government disagrees with their policies.
The national government should have the final say when regional and national governments disagree over who has authority to make a decision.
A state or region should be allowed to leave a country or federal union if a majority of its voters supports leaving in a referendum.
The national government should be able to overturn a regional policy that obstructs a nationwide programme, even if the policy has regional voter support.
States and regions should be able to adopt their own constitutions defining how their governments work, within the rights protected by the national constitution.
Police forces should be directed by a single national authority rather than by separate state or regional governments.
State and local governments should keep most of the tax revenue collected in their area rather than send it to the national government to allocate.
The national government should decide what all school pupils must study, even if regions want different compulsory subjects.
Regional governments should be able to raise or lower their own tax rates, even if this means people pay different rates in different parts of the country.
Employment laws should be set nationally, even if states or regions want different rules on working hours or dismissal.
Local voters should be able to change the powers and boundaries of their councils without national approval.
The national government should decide which medical treatments public healthcare covers, even if regional governments would cover different treatments.
Indigenous communities should be able to govern local affairs within their territories through their own institutions rather than through national authorities.
The national government should set limits on how states and regions can compete with each other through lower taxes.
Regional governments should decide how to manage land and wildlife when the effects of those decisions stay within their region.
During a disaster affecting several regions, the national government should direct the emergency response, even if regional authorities prefer their own plans.
People’s behaviour is shaped more by upbringing and social surroundings than by inherited tendencies.
Differences in IQ scores between countries can be explained more by inherited characteristics than by upbringing and education.
Where men and women behave differently, social expectations and upbringing explain more of the difference than biology does.
Differences in people’s sensitivity to stress are explained more by biological differences than by social surroundings and experience.
Differences in people’s interests are shaped more by experiences and opportunities than by inherited tendencies.
People’s willingness to take risks is shaped more by inherited tendencies than by learning and experience.
Whether people develop cooperative habits depends more on their social surroundings than on inherited tendencies.
Differences in people’s capacity for empathy are explained more by inherited characteristics than by social experience and upbringing.
Differences in people’s ability to sustain attention are explained more by their experiences and surroundings than by inherited characteristics.
People’s immediate reactions to what they consider right or wrong are shaped more by biological predispositions than by upbringing and culture.
Differences in what people find threatening are explained more by learning and experience than by inherited tendencies.
Differences in people’s temperament are explained more by biological predispositions than by upbringing and social surroundings.
People’s preferences about physical attractiveness are shaped more by culture and personal experience than by inherited tendencies.
Different races being more likely to commit violent acts (per capita) is better explained by biological differences than by upbringing and social surroundings.
People’s habits of self-control are shaped more by learning and experience than by inherited racial tendencies.
The gender pay gap can be attributed to differences in economic value between men and women instead of different social expectations.
